extractor.note: Partial pass over the Tenth, Thirteenth, Fourteenth, Twenty-sixth and Twenty-seventh Lectures.

coverage_note: Covers the Tenth Lecture (the Cartesian Meditations), the Thirteenth (empiricist prejudices), the Fourteenth (the exemplariness of natural science), the Twenty-sixth (the positively constructing line) and the Twenty-seventh (metaphysics and theory of cognition). The Ninth, Eleventh and Seventeenth Lectures and the remaining lectures carrying hits are not covered.

units.claim: Transcendental research may in principle not let the being-pre-given of objects count, treating their being-there as a problem of constitution rather than a premise.
units.quote: To "not let pre-givenness count" is the methodological refusal — the seed of the *epoché* — to take the being-there of objects as a premise rather than as itself a problem of constitution.

units.claim: Pure inner experience requires a proper method, the method of the phenomenological reduction, in order to come about at all and to keep its purity scientifically secured.
units.quote: in order to come about at all, to obtain its purity, and to carry with itself scientific security of the preservation of this purity, *a proper method, the method of the phenomenological reduction*

units.claim: The reduction is named as the still-outstanding remedy for the historical failure of inner description, whose observers' findings never harmonized.
units.quote: having named the phenomenological reduction as the still-outstanding remedy

units.term: reduction of all cognition-problems to inner experience
units.claim: Once Locke's confusion of sensation and reflection is clarified, his procedure is to be designated as the reduction of all cognition-problems to the ground of inner or consciousness-experience.
units.quote: the Lockean procedure is to be designated, in the right sense, as the *reduction of all cognition-problems to the ground of inner experience, of pure idea-experience or consciousness-experience*

units.claim: After the methodical bringing-into-relief of the phenomenological reduction as the universal ground of research, the whole work is carried out within the phenomenological attitude itself.
units.quote: Although, after the methodical bringing-into-relief of the universal ground of phenomenological research (the phenomenological reduction), this whole work carries itself out *within the phenomenological attitude itself*

units.claim: The genuine method requires that all cognition be set up merely as phenomenon and that nothing be posited first but the absolutely evident transcendental subjectivity.
units.quote: all cognition, beginning from the simple experience-cognition up to all science, must be treated as *epistemologically questionable*, and according to the sense of this questionability all and every cognition

units.claim: Everything pre-given, the sense-world and the science determining it, may only be posited as experienced of the experiencing.
units.quote: everything pre-given however self-evidently — the sense-world and the science determining it — may *only* be posited as *experienced of the experiencing*
